_why: Per-chunk gzipped budgets, checked by scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs after a build. Lighthouse audits pages and cannot reach a route behind Keycloak, which is every route in this application except /login; this reaches every chunk. Numbers are what each chunk measured when the budget was added, plus 2% rounded up - enough that an ordinary edit does not fail the build, not enough to absorb a new dependency. Never raise one to make a build pass.

_notes.exceljs.min.js: MUI X Premium's Excel export, a direct dependency of @mui/x-data-grid-premium. Lazy - nobody fetches it unless they export - but it is 23% of everything this application ships. It leaves entirely on DataGridPro, which is worth measuring against what Premium features the grids actually use.
_notes.rasterizeHTML.js: Pulled in by the grid's print export. Not obviously load-bearing - worth checking whether print is reachable at all.
_notes.totalBytes: 1199 KB measured on MUI 9.4.0 / MUI X 9.13.0, after lodash left: a 25,990-byte gzipped drop for five call sites, and the budget is RATCHETED DOWN to match rather than left with the slack in it. The previous baseline was 1211 KB on 9.3.1 / 9.12.0 - the bump cost 5 KB gzipped, and these numbers were re-derived as part of it rather than raised later under pressure. the discovery UI holds 900 KB, which is the number to aim at rather than to declare: this app ships MUI X Premium's grid, charts and pickers where it ships one grid.
_notes.application.js: Grew 4.2 KB gzipped for the display preferences: the store, the theme provider, the settings controls and the typeface registry. A deliberate addition, re-derived here rather than raised later under pressure.
_notes.useThemeStore.css: The application's stylesheet, INCLUDING the @font-face rules for all five typefaces - which cost 317 bytes gzipped between them, because a variable font's @font-face is small and the 892 KB of woff2 beside it is only fetched when a family is actually painted. The name is rolldown's, derived from whichever module anchors the chunk; it changed from application.css when the entry graph did. A rename shows up here as one chunk unbudgeted and another no longer built, which is noisy but not wrong.
_notes.i18n.js: The translation catalogue, which this branch's Insights strings pushed past the 15000 split threshold into a chunk of its own. It was inside application.js on main, and application.js is 497 bytes smaller here, so the initial load did not grow - the catalogue simply became a parallel request. Raised from 18600 to 19300 on 2026-09-25, re-derived from 18888 measured: the announcements feature adds fifteen keys and its form help text, plus three methodology strings for the walk-up metric. Strings are the one thing in this chunk, so a feature that speaks to the reader lands here by construction. Raised from 19300 to 19900 on 2026-10-10, re-derived from 19431 measured: the pre-release QA pass adds 43 strings and removes none - refusal and failure messages that replaced raw errors, accessible names for controls that had none, step and result-count announcements, and the announcements page's states.
_notes.schemas.js: Raised from 16300 to 17600 on 2026-09-23, re-derived from 17254 measured. Nothing under src/schemas/ changed: this chunk is zod's runtime, named after whichever module anchors it. insightsSearch.ts reads the Insights view out of the URL with .enum, .catch, .date, .coerce.number and .transform, and those retain more of zod than anything in the app used before. It is what validateSearch costs, and what it buys is a link that opens on the sender's view rather than the recipient's default.
_notes.insights.js: Raised from 128500 to 134300 on 2026-09-23, re-derived from 131663 measured: +5598 gzipped against main for what feat/insights-ia adds to this one route - five subjects behind a sticky bar with the whole view in the URL, the trend strip and the duration trends, loading/failed/empty/retry as four states rather than two, the metric registry that makes every figure state where it came from, and CSV export. The alternative considered and NOT taken was React.lazy on the eleven chart panels, which would move @mui/x-charts-pro out of this chunk: this repository has no lazy component anywhere yet, so that is a pattern to introduce deliberately rather than under budget pressure, and it defers bytes rather than removing any. The total still has 10575 bytes to spare.
_notes.axios.js: Raised from 18100 to 19000 on 2026-10-10, re-derived from 18583 measured: axios 1.19.0 -> 1.20.0 clears twelve advisories (npm audit, high), and the fix costs 483 bytes gzipped. The cut that would remove this chunk entirely is replacing axios with fetch at its 17 REST call sites; graphql-request already uses fetch.
_notes.CombinedRequestingModal.js: Raised from 15800 to 16300 on 2026-10-10, re-derived from 15918 measured: the request dialogs now say why a request was refused, announce each step, validate the patron on Enter, stop polling on failure and fetch the due date after checkout.
_notes.dateTimeRangeOperators.js: New name, not new weight: added 2026-10-10 at 15573 measured, plus 2%. Filter-operator code shared by six column definitions, regrouped by rolldown once the operator labels were translated. The total measured 1247474, 743 bytes above main's 1246731, after the QA pass's 43 strings, axios bump and new error states.
